answers.answer: To save a quote on the page: open Quotes, choose New quote, type the line in Quote, optionally fill Said by, Game and Said at, then choose Add quote. The quote then appears at the top of the list with its number. In chat, type !quote add followed by the line, or reply to a message with !quote add. To get a quote back, type !quote 12 in chat, use Search the quotes on the page, or choose Random quote.
answers.quote: Open Quotes and choose New quote.

answers.answer: You need the right role. Out of the box, VIP and up may add and edit, and Moderator and up may delete. Anyone in chat can read a quote with !quote. The opening section and its permissions table state this.
answers.quote: By default, everyone in chat can read a quote with !quote, and the Quotes page is for VIP and up.

answers.answer: After you save, the dialog closes and the quote appears at the top of the list with its new number. In chat, the bot's reply shows the number, such as #12.
answers.quote: The dialog closes, and the quote shows at the top of the list with its new number.

answers.answer: The moderator chooses the pencil button on the quote's row, or searches for an older quote first, changes the text and chooses Save quote. Another way is to type !quote edit 12 followed by the new line in chat. The number never changes, so !quote 12 still finds the corrected quote. A chat edit also keeps Said by, Game and Said at. On the page, leaving Said at empty keeps the date the quote already had.
answers.quote: The bot numbers each quote for you, and that number stays with the quote for good, so !quote 12 keeps finding the same line after you fix a typo in it.

answers.answer: A small detour: the Edit section says the list shows the newest 100 quotes, but only the Find section explains that the list starts at 50 and needs Show more quotes to reach 100. This costs a moment of rereading and blocks no step.
answers.quote: The list shows only the newest 100 quotes, so for an older quote, search for it first to bring up its row.

answers.answer: Nothing read aloud is confusing enough to stop a task. The four sentences about time zones for Said at are dense, but each one is something a reader acts on.
answers.quote: Said at is stored as one moment in time: you pick it in your own computer’s time zone, and each person who opens the page sees the date in their own time zone.

warning_review.reason: Word count of a full reference-style page. Every section answers a question the reader asks (add, edit, delete, find, random, chat, cooldown), and the blind pass answered all six questions without a stall. A count alone is not a defect.

The access rules (VIP and up to add, Moderator and up to delete) and the field table come before the steps because the steps depend on them. Moving them lower would send the reader into the steps without knowing whether they may act or what to fill in.
The fact that the number never changes is what makes !quote 12 a reliable reference after a fix. The length carries one consequence, and the blind pass found the answer in it at once.
This is a surprise a VIP would otherwise hit: a !quote reply saves a message instead of reading one. The clause naming the default role is needed to know whether it applies, so the length is kept.
Time zone handling is a fact the reader cannot assume and acts on when picking a date. The blind answer noted the density, but each clause is a fact that affects the step, so the wording stays.
A deleted quote's number is not reused, so a later chat lookup of that number fails. A moderator deleting a quote needs to know that the number will not return another line.
A sentence count only. The sentences in the paragraph are facts the reader acts on, per the blind answers, so the wording stays.

A VIP who saves by mistake needs the moderator removal path and the interim edit path in one place. Splitting it would add a second sentence with the same subject; the length is the cost of two actions and does not block the reader.
